newsitem.title: USA: Strike threat cuts further into UPS deliveries.
newsitem.headline: Strike threat cuts further into UPS deliveries.

text.p: More than a day after the Teamsters postponed a strike, United Parcel Service, the largest U.S. package carrier, said it was losing about 8 percent of its daily business.

"We're up to losing 1 million packages a day," UPS spokeswoman Gina Ellrich said, adding that the loss amounted to about $5 million a day. The company normally delivers about 12 million packages daily.
The decline grew from hundreds of thousands of packages earlier in the week as a strike deadline approached and passed Thursday night and the company told customers it could not guarantee service.

"The trend that we've seen from our customers (is) the closer we got to the deadline the more they diverted their volume," she said. "We think the more tenuous it is the more we will see that happen."
A Teamsters Union spokesman on Friday called the company's statement about the drop in business a "scare tactic" but said UPS had brought the problem on itself.
UPS and the union temporarily suspended talks on Friday after meeting all day with federal mediators in an effort to avert a strike.

The union, which represents about 200,000 UPS workers who drive, load and sort packages, is pressing the company to create more full-time jobs, stop subcontracting, and improve safety, health and pension conditions.
Ellrich said negotiations were unlikely to resume this weekend. "We don't have any indication on when they will resume," she said. "We probably won't see anything till Monday."
UPS said it had already had to lay off hundreds of workers temporarily.

The Teamsters issued a statement on Friday saying the London-based International Transport Workers Federation stood ready to launch a worldwide campaign in solidarity with UPS workers if they went on strike.

UPS is the largest package carrier in the United States, with 1996 revenues of $22.4 billion. It handles 3.15 billion parcels and documents, shipped annually to more than 200 countries from 1,700 hubs and centres.
Teamster officials and federal mediators were not immediately available for comment.
